diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the same table twice sequentially (99K rows each) and then performs a hash-based deduplication (HASH_GROUP_BY) on the combined ~198K rows, causing high I/O and CPU for duplicate elimination.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

The HASH_GROUP_BY (deduplication) processes nearly 200K input rows with high overlap, requiring hash table build/probe and memory; reducing input cardinality or avoiding the second scan would cut its cost.
The first SEQ_SCAN reads the entire trips table to filter trip_distance>30; an index on trip_distance could turn this into an index scan with far fewer rows read.

The second SEQ_SCAN reads the entire trips table again to filter fare_amount>100; an index on fare_amount or a single combined scan (trip_distance>30 OR fare_amount>100) would eliminate the double scan.
